style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">We maintain 401(k) Savings Plans for substantially all of our full-time employees. A percentage of employee contributions are matched through an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) contribution or cash contribution up to certain limits. Certain union employees receive a contribution to their ESOP account regardless of their participation in the 401(k) Savings Plan. The ESOP held </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">3.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares of our common stock (market value of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$206.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">) at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. Certain employees participate in a defined contribution pension plan, in which certain amounts are contributed to an employee's account based on the employee's wages, age, and years of service. Total costs incurred under all of these plans were </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$36.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$19.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$17.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">We maintain deferred compensation plans that enable certain key employees and nonemployee directors to defer payment of a portion of their compensation or fees on a pre-tax basis. Nonemployee directors can defer up to </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">100%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of their director fees. Compensation is generally deferred in the form of cash and is indexed to certain investment options or our common stock. The deemed dividends paid on our common stock are automatically reinvested. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The deferred compensation arrangements for which distributions are made solely in our common stock are classified as an equity instrument on the balance sheets. Changes in the fair value of this portion of the deferred compensation obligation are not recognized. The deferred compensation obligation classified as an equity instrument was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$24.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$23.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The portion of the deferred compensation obligation that is indexed to various investment options and allows for distributions in cash is classified as a liability on the balance sheets. The liability is adjusted, with a charge or credit to expense, to reflect changes in the fair value of the deferred compensation obligation. The obligation classified within other long-term liabilities was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$53.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$42.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The costs incurred under this arrangement were </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$6.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$3.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$2.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The deferred compensation programs are partially funded through shares of our common stock that are held in a rabbi trust. holding company to pay dividends is largely dependent upon the availability of funds from our subsidiaries. Various laws, regulations, and financial covenants impose restrictions on the ability of certain of our regulated utility subsidiaries to transfer funds to us in the form of dividends. Our regulated utility subsidiaries, with the exception of MGU, are prohibited from loaning funds to us, either directly or indirectly.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The PSCW allows WPS to pay dividends on its common stock of no more than </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">103%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the previous year&#8217;s common stock dividend. WPS may return capital to us if its average financial common equity ratio is at least </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">51%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;on a calendar-year basis. WPS must obtain PSCW approval if a return of capital would cause its average financial common equity ratio to fall below this level. Our right to receive dividends on the common stock of WPS is also subject to the prior rights of WPS&#8217;s preferred shareholders and to provisions in WPS&#8217;s restated articles of incorporation, which limit the amount of common stock dividends that WPS may pay if its common stock and common stock surplus accounts constitute less than </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">25%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of its total capitalization.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">NSG&#8217;s long-term debt obligations contain provisions and covenants restricting the payment of cash dividends and the purchase or redemption of its capital stock.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">PGL and WPS have short-term debt obligations containing financial and other covenants, including but not limited to, a requirement to maintain a debt to total capitalization ratio not to exceed </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">65%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. style="line-height:120%;font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In 2012,&#160;ITF formed AMP Trillium LLC as a joint venture with AMP Americas LLC. ITF owns </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">30%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and AMP Americas LLC owns </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">70%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the joint venture. The joint venture was established to own and operate compressed natural gas fueling stations. The preferred source of capital funding for the joint venture is loans from ITF. We determined that the joint venture is a variable interest entity and that ITF is the primary beneficiary, which requires us to consolidate the assets, liabilities, and statements of income of the joint venture. At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, our variable interests in the joint venture included an insignificant equity investment and insignificant receivables. Our maximum exposure to loss as a result of this joint venture was not significant. The carrying amounts of AMP Trillium LLC assets and liabilities included on our balance sheets were also not significant.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In 2011,&#160;ITF formed Integrys PTI CNG Fuels LLC as a joint venture with Paper Transport Inc. The joint venture was established to own and operate compressed natural gas fueling stations. ITF and Paper Transport Inc. each initially owned </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the joint venture. We determined that the joint venture is a variable interest entity and that ITF was the primary beneficiary, which required us to consolidated the assets, liabilities, and statements of income of the joint venture. At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, our variable interests in the joint venture included an insignificant equity investment and insignificant receivables. The carrying amounts of Integrys PTI CNG Fuels LLC assets and liabilities included on our December 31, 2012, balance sheet were also not significant. In June 2013, ITF purchased Paper Transport Inc.'s </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;ownership interest of the joint venture, and it became a wholly owned subsidiary.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Unconsolidated Variable Interest Entities</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In 2013,&#160;ITF formed EVO Trillium LLC as a joint venture with Environmental Alternative Fuels LLC. ITF owns </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">15%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and Environmental Alternative Fuels LLC owns </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">85%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the joint venture. This joint venture was established to own and operate compressed natural gas fueling stations. We determined that this joint venture is a variable interest entity but that consolidation is not required since we are not its primary beneficiary, as we don't have the power to direct its activities. We instead account for this variable interest entity as an equity method investment. At December&#160;31, 2013, the </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">94</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><br><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:13px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">assets and liabilities on our balance sheet related to our involvement with this variable interest entity consisted of insignificant receivables. Our maximum exposure to loss as a result of involvement with this variable interest entity was also not significant. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">We have a variable interest in an entity through a power purchase agreement at UPPCO that reimburses an independent power producing entity for coal costs relating to purchased energy. There is </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">no</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;obligation to purchase energy under this agreement. This contract for </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">17.5</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;megawatts of capacity expires in 2014. For a variety of reasons, including qualitative factors such as the length of the remaining term of the contract compared with the remaining life of the plant and the fact that we do not have the power to direct the operations and maintenance of the facility, we determined we are not the primary beneficiary of this variable interest entity and that consolidation is not required. At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2012</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the assets and liabilities on our balance sheets that related to our involvement with this variable interest entity pertained to working capital accounts and represented the amounts we owed for current deliveries of power. We have not guaranteed any debt or provided any equity support, liquidity arrangements, performance guarantees, or other commitments associated with the contract. Our maximum exposure to loss as a result of involvement with this variable interest entity was not significant.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">We also had a variable interest in Fox Energy Company LLC through a power purchase agreement at WPS that contained a tolling arrangement related to the cost of fuel. In connection with the purchase of Fox Energy Company LLC in March 2013, WPS paid </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$50.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for the early termination of this </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">500</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-megawatt agreement. </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">See Note 3, Acquisitions, for more information</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;regarding this purchase. We evaluated this variable interest entity for possible consolidation and determined that consolidation was not required since we were not the primary beneficiary of the variable interest entity. The assets and liabilities on our December 31, 2012, balance sheet that related to our involvement with this variable interest entity pertained to working capital accounts and represented the amounts we owed for current deliveries of power. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><a #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><a name="s6ED74DB78B4B77B3DB8B38B3760D504F"></a><div style="line-height:120%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 26&#8212;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory Environment</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Wisconsin</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2014 Rates </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2013, the PSCW issued a final written order for WPS, effective January 1, 2014. It authorized a net retail electric rate decrease of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$12.8&#160;million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and a net retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$4.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, reflecting a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10.20%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity. The order also included a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50.14%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in WPS's regulatory capital structure. The retail electric rate impact consists of a rate increase, offset by a portion of estimated fuel cost over-collections from customers in 2013 of the same amount. Retail electric rates were further decreased by 2012 decoupling over-collections to be returned to customers in 2014. Additionally, the retail electric rate decrease includes the deferral of the difference between the 2012 fuel refund and the 2013 rate increase discussed below. The retail natural gas rate impact consists of a rate decrease, which was more than offset by the positive impact of 2012 decoupling under-collections to be recovered from customers in 2014. Both the retail electric and retail natural gas rate changes include the recovery of pension and other employee benefit increases that were deferred in the 2013 rate case, as discussed below. The PSCW also authorized the recovery of prudently incurred 2014 environmental mitigation project costs related to compliance with a Consent Decree signed in January 2013 related to the Pulliam and Weston sites. </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">See Note 15, Commitments and Contingencies, for more information</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. Additionally, the order requires WPS to terminate its existing decoupling mechanism, beginning January 1, 2014</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2013 Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2012, the PSCW issued a final written order for WPS, effective January 1, 2013. The order included a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$28.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;retail electric rate increase, partially offset by the actual 2012 fuel refund of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$20.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The difference between the 2012 fuel refund and the rate increase was deferred for recovery in 2014 rates. As a result, there was no change to customers' 2013 retail electric rates. The order also included a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$3.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;retail natural gas rate decrease. The rate changes included deferrals of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$7.3 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for retail electric and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$2.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for retail natural gas of pension and other employee benefit costs that are being recovered in 2014 rates. The order reflected a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10.30%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">51.61%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in WPS's regulatory capital structure. In addition, WPS was authorized recovery of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$5.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;related to income tax amounts previously expensed due to the Federal Health Care Reform Act. As a result, this amount was recorded as a regulatory asset in 2012, and recovery from customers began in 2013. The order also authorized the recovery of direct Cross State Air Pollution Rule (CSAPR) costs incurred through the end of 2012. Lastly, the order authorized WPS to switch from production tax credits to Section 1603 Grants for the Crane Creek wind project.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">A new decoupling mechanism for natural gas and electric residential and small commercial and industrial customers was approved on a pilot basis as part of the order. The mechanism was based on total rate case-approved margins, rather than being calculated on a per-customer basis. The mechanism did not cover all customer classes, and it continued to include an annual </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$14.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cap for electric service and an annual </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$8.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cap for natural gas service. Amounts recoverable from or refundable to customers were subject to these caps. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2012 Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2011, the PSCW issued a final written order for WPS, effective January 1, 2012. The order authorized a retail electric rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$8.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and required a retail natural gas rate decrease of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$7.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The retail electric rate increase was driven by projected increases in fuel and purchased power costs. However, to the extent that actual fuel and purchased power costs exceeded a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;variance from costs included in rates, they were deferred for recovery or refund in a future rate proceeding. The rate order allowed for the netting of the 2010 electric decoupling under-collection with the 2011 electric decoupling over-collection and reflected reduced contributions to the Focus on Energy Program. The rate order also allowed for the deferral of direct CSAPR compliance costs, including carrying costs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">99</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><a style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;" href="#sA14A332CD95B25A64F5F38B38830E36C"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Michigan</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2014 MGU Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In November 2013, the MPSC issued a final written order for MGU, effective January 1, 2014. The order authorized a retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$4.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The rates reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10.25%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">48.62%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in MGU's regulatory capital structure. Additionally, the order requires MGU to terminate its existing decoupling mechanism after December&#160;31, 2013, and replace it with a new decoupling mechanism based on total margins, beginning January 1, 2015. The new decoupling mechanism will not cover variations in volumes due to actual weather being different from rate case-assumed weather. The rate order also terminates MGU's existing uncollectible expense true-up mechanism after December 31, 2013. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">MGU Depreciation Case</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In January 2013, the Michigan Court of Appeals issued an order reversing the MPSC's 2010 disallowance of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$2.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;associated with the early retirement of certain MGU assets. As a result, a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$2.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;reduction to depreciation expense was recorded in the first quarter of 2013. In June 2013, the MPSC issued an order related to MGU's most recent depreciation case. This order also approved a settlement agreement reflecting recovery of these previously disallowed costs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2014 UPPCO Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2013, the MPSC issued a final written order for UPPCO, effective January 1, 2014. The order authorized a retail electric rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$5.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The rates reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10.15%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">56.74%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in UPPCO's regulatory capital structure. The order requires UPPCO to terminate its existing decoupling mechanism after December&#160;31, 2013. In addition, the order requires UPPCO to achieve certain minimum line clearance performance metrics for recovery of costs related to clearing trees and other natural obstructions away from power lines. If these metrics are not achieved, or if the minimum spending level is not reached, the company may be required to refund certain amounts to customers.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2012 UPPCO Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2011, the MPSC issued a final written order for UPPCO, effective January 1, 2012. The order authorized a retail electric rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$4.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The rates reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10.20%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">54.90%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in UPPCO's regulatory capital structure. The order stated that if UPPCO filed a rate case in 2013, the earliest effective date for new final rates or self-implemented rates would be January 1, 2014. Additionally, the order required UPPCO to terminate its existing decoupling mechanism, effective December&#160;31, 2011, and replace it with a new decoupling mechanism based on total margins, beginning January 1, 2013. The new decoupling mechanism does not cover variations in volumes due to actual weather being different from rate case-assumed weather. It includes an annual </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">1.5%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cap based on distribution revenues approved in the rate case. UPPCO had no decoupling mechanism in place during 2012.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In April 2012, the State of Michigan Court of Appeals ruled in a Detroit Edison proceeding that the MPSC did not have authority to approve electric decoupling mechanisms. This decision was not appealed. As a result of this ruling, UPPCO expensed </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$1.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in the first quarter of 2012 related to electric decoupling amounts previously deferred for regulatory recovery. However, in August&#160;2012, the MPSC issued an order stating it had the authority to approve UPPCO's decoupling mechanism, as UPPCO's decoupling mechanism was authorized pursuant to an MPSC-approved settlement agreement. Therefore, in the third quarter of 2012, UPPCO reversed the </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$1.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;previously expensed in the first quarter of 2012.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Illinois</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2015 Rate Cases</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In February 2014, PGL and NSG filed applications with the ICC to increase retail natural gas rates </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">$128.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">$7.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, with rates expected to be effective in early 2015. Both PGL's and NSG's requests reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">10.25%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity. The requests reflect a target common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;">50.41%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for NSG and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">50.31%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for PGL in their respective regulatory capital structures. The proposed retail natural gas rate increases are primarily driven by increased capital investments, in particular for main replacement, a loss in revenues as a result of lower projected sales volumes, increased costs of debt and common equity, and increased operating expenses. The increase in operating expenses relates to pipeline safety and other compliance work, a general wage increase, higher depreciation costs, and higher invested capital taxes. PGL's application also includes adjustments for the effects of its new Qualifying Infrastructure Plant rider, as discussed below. PGL and NSG proposed no changes to the continued use of their decoupling mechanisms and uncollectible expense true-up mechanisms. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">Qualifying Infrastructure Plant (QIP) Rider</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In July 2013, Illinois Public Act 98-0057 (formerly Senate Bill 2266), The Natural Gas Consumer, Safety &amp; Reliability Act, became law. The Act gives PGL a cost recovery mechanism for Illinois natural gas infrastructure upgrades that will be collected through a surcharge on customer bills. Later in July 2013, the ICC adopted emergency rules to implement the law, and in December 2013, issued an order to adopt permanent rules replacing the </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">100</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><a style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;" href="#sA14A332CD95B25A64F5F38B38830E36C"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">emergency rules. This Act eliminated a requirement for PGL and NSG to file biennial rate proceedings under existing Illinois coal-to-gas legislation. In September 2013, PGL filed with the ICC requesting the proposed rider, and the ICC approved the tariff in January 2014. The rider became effective on January 1, 2014.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2013 Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In June 2013, the ICC issued a final written order for PGL and NSG, effective June 27, 2013. The order authorized a retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$57.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for PGL and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$6.6 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for NSG. The rates for PGL reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">9.28%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50.43%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in its regulatory capital structure. The rates for NSG reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">9.28%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50.32%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in its regulatory capital structure. The rate order also allowed PGL and NSG to continue the use of their decoupling mechanisms, as affirmed by the Illinois Appellate Court (Court). </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In August 2013, the ICC granted certain rehearing requests on tax-related issues filed by PGL, NSG, and other intervenors. PGL and NSG asked for a correction of the revenue requirement for deferred tax assets related to tax net operating losses (NOLs) incurred in 2012 and 2013.&#160;In the ICC&#8217;s order, these deferred tax assets were included in rate base, but computational errors were made.&#160;Other intervenors requested the exclusion from rate base of the deferred tax asset related to the 2012 tax NOL.&#160;The tax NOLs in question resulted from PGL and NSG claiming accelerated depreciation deductions in 2012 and 2013. In December 2013, the ICC evaluated and approved a correction of the computational errors and rejected the intervenors' proposed exclusion of the 2012 tax NOL. Customer rates were increased by </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$2.6 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for PGL and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$0.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for NSG for the impact of this correction, effective January&#160;1, 2014. In January 2014, the Illinois Attorney General and Citizens Utility Board each filed an appeal with the Court.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2012 Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In January 2012, the ICC issued a final written order, effective January 21, 2012. The order authorized a retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$57.8&#160;million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for PGL and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$1.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;for NSG. The rates for PGL reflected a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">9.45%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">49.00%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in PGL's regulatory capital structure. The rates for NSG reflected a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">9.45%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50.00%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in NSG's regulatory capital structure. The rate order also approved a permanent decoupling mechanism.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Illinois Attorney General and Citizens Utility Board appealed to the Court the ICC's authority to approve PGL's and NSG's decoupling mechanisms and filed a motion to stay the implementation of the permanent decoupling mechanism or make collections subject to refund. In May 2012, the ICC issued a revised amendatory order granting the Illinois Attorney General's motion to make revenues collected under the permanent decoupling mechanism subject to refund. Refunds would have been required if the Court found that the ICC did not have authority to approve decoupling and ordered a refund. As a result, the recovery of amounts related to decoupling in 2012 were uncertain, and PGL and NSG established offsetting reserves equal to decoupling amounts accrued. In March 2013, the Court issued an opinion that affirmed the ICC's order approving the permanent decoupling mechanism. As a result, the reserves recorded in 2012 were reversed in the first quarter of 2013. PGL's and NSG's permanent decoupling mechanism was in place for 2013. In June 2013, the Illinois Attorney General and Citizens Utility Board petitioned the Illinois Supreme Court to appeal the Court's decision. The Illinois Supreme Court granted the request in September 2013. The Illinois Supreme Court has no deadline by which it must act. Decoupling amounts recorded in 2012 were fully recovered and amounts in 2013 will be refunded to customers in 2014. Decoupling amounts in 2014 will continue to be accrued, absent an adverse Illinois Supreme Court decision. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Minnesota</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2014 Rate Case</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In September 2013, MERC filed an application with the MPUC to increase retail natural gas distribution rates by </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$14.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. MERC's request reflects a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">10.75%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">50.31%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in its regulatory capital structure. The request was primarily driven by general inflation, property taxes, improvements to customer service programs, efforts to expand the customer base which would have a positive rate effect in the future, and operating and maintenance projects to ensure reliability and safety for customers. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2013, the MPUC approved an interim rate order authorizing MERC a retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$10.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, effective January&#160;1, 2014. The interim rates reflect a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">9.70%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">50.31%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in MERC's regulatory capital structure. The interim rate increase is subject to refund pending the final rate order, which is expected in the fourth quarter of 2014. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">2011 Rates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In July 2012, the MPUC approved a final written order for MERC, effective January 1, 2013. The order authorized a retail natural gas rate increase of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$11.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. The rates reflected a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">9.70%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;return on common equity and a common equity ratio of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">50.48%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in MERC's regulatory capital structure. In addition, the order set recovery of MERC's 2011 test-year pension expense at 2010 levels. The MPUC also approved a decoupling mechanism for MERC that covers residential and small commercial and industrial customers on a </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">three</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year trial basis, effective January 1, 2013. The decoupling mechanism does not adjust for variations in volumes resulting from changes in customer count compared to rate case levels. It includes an annual </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cap based on distribution revenues approved in the rate case. Amounts recoverable from or refundable to customers are subject to this cap.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the financial statements and financial statement schedules based on our audits.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.
